items.title: Personalize IGNIS starters by vs_last_game signal
items.why: The 5 starter prompts are static for all visitors, but vs_last_game (set in S212 W3 by ambient-loader.js) already knows whether this person last played Call of Doodie, Football GM, or Forge. A returning CoD player who opens IGNIS and sees 'What makes Call of Doodie different?' converts the warm session signal into immediate relevance — no typing needed. This closes the S212 personalization loop: the game-visit tracking exists, the starters exist, but they never talk to each other.
items.recipe: Read localStorage.getItem('vs_last_game') at renderStarters() time; swap in 1–2 game-specific questions for the matching slug (cod/fgm/forge) while keeping 3 general starters. Add data-slug attr on each button for L3 analytics merge.
items.premiseVerified: CONFIRMED: line 184–216 ignis-answer-engine.js — STARTERS array is a static 5-string literal; vs_last_game is never read in this function. The game tracking IIFE in ambient-loader.js writes cod/fgm/forge but ignis-answer-engine.js never reads it.

L1.recipe: Read vs_last_game at mount; prepend 1 game-specific starter before the 5 general ones. Minimal code delta, immediate personalization lift.

L2.recipe: Full 3-game starter packs (3 game-specific + 2 general when vs_last_game set). Add data-slug attribute to each button for analytics merge (completes ignis-starter-analytics L2).

L3.recipe: Topic-history analysis: parse vs_ignis_history query list for recurring terms (game names, features), weight matching starters higher. Requires a topic-extractor helper; no backend.

items.title: Replace static no-result fallback with dynamic cluster suggestions
items.why: When IGNIS finds no strong match it shows a hardcoded string: 'Try membership, latest ships, security, Oracle, or a game name.' These 4 suggestions were written months ago and may not reflect what's actually in the current 44,691-entry index. A dynamic fallback that pulls the top clusters from api/oracle-query-clusters.json stays current, surfaces what visitors actually search for, and emits an oracle:no_result RUM event — closing the only gap in the IGNIS observability loop (successes are measured, failures are invisible).
items.recipe: At the !result branch (line 302 ignis-answer-engine.js), load api/oracle-query-clusters.json and surface the top 3 cluster labels as tappable suggestion chips. Emit oracle:no_result RUM on each zero-result query.
items.premiseVerified: CONFIRMED: line 302 ignis-answer-engine.js — literal string 'IGNIS did not find a strong public match yet. Try "membership"...' is the only no-result path. api/oracle-query-clusters.json exists (built by build-oracle-query-clusters.mjs). No oracle:no_result event exists in Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS.

L1.recipe: Replace static string with random selection from the 5 existing STARTERS queries as fallback suggestions — no network request, instant improvement.

L2.recipe: Fetch api/oracle-query-clusters.json (already on CDN), render top 3 cluster chip buttons. Add oracle:no_result to Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS so zero-result rate is measurable.

L3.recipe: Intent-pivot: detect query entity type (name vs. question vs. keyword), offer reformulation hints ('Did you mean: ...?') using tokenized index title prefix matching. Surface most similar doc title as a rescue link.

items.title: Add slug suffix to oracle:starter_click RUM for per-starter attribution
items.why: oracle:starter_click fires for all 5 starters identically — the studio can count how many starter clicks happen but cannot tell which starter drives engagement. This matters because the S212 bet is that certain starters create a stronger IGNIS habit loop. Without per-starter attribution the personalization planned in ignis-starter-personalization has no feedback signal to prove which game-specific questions work best.
items.recipe: Change onClick to emit('oracle:starter_click:' + slugify(q)) where slugify converts the question to a lowercase-hyphen key. Add prefixAllowlist('oracle:starter_click', ...) to Worker. In the rollup, track per-slug counts in api/oracle-starter-insights.json.
items.premiseVerified: CONFIRMED: line 209 ignis-answer-engine.js — emitUx('oracle:starter_click') has no slug. slugify helper already exists in ignis-answer-engine.js (used for cluster IDs). prefixAllowlist pattern already established (see S192 oracle:feedback_submitted).

L1.recipe: Emit oracle:starter_click:<slug> (5 bounded values), add prefixAllowlist entry in Worker. Rollup counts per slug appear in funnel-summary families.

L2.recipe: Also track position (0–4) and whether the query produced a result: oracle:starter_click:<slug>:hit vs :miss. This closes the starter→answer→conversion funnel.

L3.recipe: Build scripts/build-oracle-starter-insights.mjs → api/oracle-starter-insights.json (per-starter click rate + hit rate + downstream query continuation rate). Feed into the personalization decision for ignis-starter-personalization.

items.title: Store game interest context in push subscription KV for segmented dispatch
items.why: The first real push dispatch (next session's headline) will blast a single message to all subscribers regardless of their interests. A CoD player who gets a Football GM update notification has a high unsubscribe risk — and unsubscribing a push subscriber is permanent. Storing the visitor's page context at subscribe time (costs 0 extra bytes in the existing KV entry) makes every future dispatch richer without requiring the visitor to do anything different.
items.recipe: In push-subscribe.js POST body, append route: location.pathname and lastGame: localStorage.getItem('vs_last_game')||null alongside sub.toJSON(). In the Worker /v/push-subscribe handler, store these in the KV value. In notify-subscribers.mjs, accept --game flag to filter by stored lastGame.
items.premiseVerified: CONFIRMED: push-subscribe.js line 60 — body is JSON.stringify(sub.toJSON()) only. No game context stored. Worker receives and stores the raw subscription JSON. notify-subscribers.mjs dispatches to all subscribers with no filtering.

L1.recipe: Store route: location.pathname in KV. dispatch --route /games/call-of-doodie/ filters to subscribers who subscribed on that page. Immediate segmentation by page context.

L2.recipe: Store lastGame field from localStorage. notify-subscribers.mjs --game cod/fgm/forge filters by stored interest. Game-specific dispatch campaigns are now possible.

L3.recipe: Multi-interest subscriber model: append gameSlug to existing interests[] array on each game page visit (requires a PATCH-style KV update on the Worker). Rich segmentation for newsletters, game updates, milestones.

items.title: Add service-worker push click → RUM beacon for delivery + open rate
items.why: The push notification pipeline can dispatch but has no visibility into whether pushes are received, opened, or clicked. The service worker receives push events and can respond to notificationclick — wiring a navigator.sendBeacon('/v/rum', ...) in the click handler closes the loop: the studio can measure open rate per campaign and compare push CTR against in-page CTAs.
items.recipe: In assets/service-worker.js (or sw.js), add a notificationclick handler that beacons push:clicked with the notification tag. Add push:clicked and push:received to Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS. Wire push:dispatched:{count} log in notify-subscribers.mjs.
items.premiseVerified: PREMISE PARTIAL: service worker exists (for PWA). notificationclick handler presence needs verification. Recipe remains valid regardless — the push event is guaranteed to fire in the SW context; click handling is additive.

L1.recipe: Log dispatch count vs subscriber count to console + a .cache/last-dispatch-log.json file. Immediate visibility without a SW change.

L2.recipe: SW notificationclick handler → sendBeacon push:clicked. Worker allowlist update. rollup push:* family in funnel-summary.

L3.recipe: Full campaign attribution: include a campaign ID in notification data → SW preserves it in the click beacon → correlate open rate + downstream membership conversion per campaign.

With the game quiz personalization (S212 W3) and IGNIS starters (S212 W4) now live, the first cohort of quiz:personalized + oracle:starter_click events should be visible in a fresh rollup.

items.premiseVerified: CONFIRMED: api/funnel-summary.json generatedAt: 2026-06-14. S212 shipped quiz:personalized + oracle:starter_click RUM events on 2026-06-20. 6-day gap confirmed.

L2.recipe: Wire rollup-rum-ux into a daily GitHub Actions step so the summary never goes stale again.

L3.recipe: Same as L2 plus a freshness check gate that fails build:check if funnel-summary is >3 days old (analogous to the perf-history freshness gate).

items.title: Derive Projects/Games nav dropdowns from catalog (carry D-S208)
items.why: The nav dropdowns for Games and Projects are currently hardcoded arrays (NAV_GAMES, NAV_PROJECTS) in propagate-nav.mjs that can drift from the catalog. S210 closed the sync gate (check-nav-catalog-sync warns on drift) but the root fix — deriving the arrays from catalog data — was deferred due to the non-catalog-paged projects complication. This carry reduces the maintenance surface permanently.
items.recipe: Design the catalog∪extra-paged merge: maintain a EXTRA_NAV_PAGES constant for non-catalog paged entries (signal-log, vault-pipeline, etc.). Derive NAV_GAMES + NAV_PROJECTS by unioning catalog SPARKED/FORGE entries with EXTRA_NAV_PAGES. Propagate to 99+ pages. Update check-nav-catalog-sync to validate the derived list.
items.premiseVerified: CONFIRMED: scripts/propagate-nav.mjs lines define NAV_GAMES + NAV_PROJECTS as hardcoded arrays. check-nav-catalog-sync.mjs advisory gate exists. Non-catalog-paged projects documented in TASK_BOARD S208 carries.

L1.recipe: Document the EXTRA_NAV_PAGES list; prove which pages are non-catalog-paged. Design the merge algorithm before writing code.

L2.recipe: Implement catalog union + EXTRA_NAV_PAGES constant in propagate-nav.mjs. Re-propagate 99 pages. Update sync gate to use the derived list.

L3.recipe: Fully data-driven: remove EXTRA_NAV_PAGES by adding a navVisible:true field to each non-catalog-paged project's page meta. All nav items derive from one structure.

items.title: Ship Ark cargo to fix VOID/SHADOW/Hashmark protocol compliance gaps
items.why: Three sibling repos (VOID, SHADOW, Hashmark) have drifted from the v3.3 protocol template — missing TRUTH_AUDIT headers, stale session templates, missing PROJECT_STATUS fields. These 3 failures drag the studio compliance score from 100% to 91% for the third consecutive day. Ark cargo of type canon-update or agent-handoff to studio-ops is the only CANON-018-compliant path to fix these without direct cross-repo writes.
items.recipe: node ../vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/ark.mjs ship --type agent-handoff --to studio-ops --payload with the specific gaps per repo. studio-ops propagation handles the template updates.
items.premiseVerified: CONFIRMED: docs/COMPLIANCE_HISTORY.md — VOID, SHADOW, Hashmark failing for 3+ days. Failures are sibling repos, not this repo. CANON-018 requires Ark. studio-ops propagation script handles template updates.

L1.recipe: Ship one Ark cargo per failing repo with the specific gap list. Studio-ops processes in next available slot.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a targeted fix payload with the exact file edits needed so studio-ops can auto-apply rather than re-diagnose.

L3.recipe: Propose a canon-update that adds a CI action to each repo that auto-validates against the v3.3 template on push — preventing future drift without manual checks.
